- \(10 = 2 \cdot 5 \;\Rightarrow\; f(10)=f(2)+f(5)=14\).
- \(40 = 2^3 \cdot 5 \;\Rightarrow\; f(40)=3f(2)+f(5)=20\).

Let \(a = f(2)\) and \(b = f(5)\). Then we have the system:
\[
\begin{cases}
a + b = 14 \\
3a + b = 20
\end{cases}
\]

Subtract the first equation from the second: \(2a = 6 \Rightarrow a = 3\). Then \(b = 14 - 3 = 11\).

Now factor \(500\) into primes:
\(500 = 2^2 \cdot 5^3\).

Thus
\[
f(500) = 2f(2)+3f(5)=2a+3b = 2(3)+3(11)=6+33=39.
\]

So \(f(500)=39\).
